options.label: Graphics backend
options.description: How Snes9x draws the picture. Vulkan and OpenGL use the GPU; Software works everywhere but is slower. XVideo is an old X11 video overlay. If a backend cannot start, Snes9x shows an error box and falls back to Software.

options.label: Aspect ratio
options.description: The picture's shape. 4:3 is how games looked on a TV. Pixel-perfect versions only enlarge by whole steps, so every pixel has the same size, and leave borders around the picture.

options.label: Screen filter
options.description: Sharp keeps crisp square pixels; Smooth blurs them slightly when the picture is enlarged.

options.label: VSync
options.description: Wait for the screen before showing each frame: no tearing, may add a little input lag. Vulkan and OpenGL only.

options.label: Input latency
options.description: Low starts each frame as late as it can still make the screen, so the game reads the controller later and a press shows up sooner (about 25 ms sooner for a light game on a 60 Hz panel). It only acts with VSync on and the Vulkan renderer, and turns itself off while frames take most of a refresh, so a heavy game is unaffected. Normal is the standard timing.

options.label: Show FPS
options.description: Draw the frame rate on the picture.

notes: Source: snes9xgit/snes9x tag 1.63 (921f9f7b83660eb44ad263022a57a4a029057c37), the GTK frontend packaged by pkgforge-dev/Snes9x-AppImage 1.63-1. Every key is in ~/.config/snes9x/snes9x.conf.

The file: Snes9x reads it once at startup (gui_config->load_config_file(), gtk/src/gtk_s9x.cpp:77) and REWRITES IT WHOLE on exit (save_config_file() from S9xExit, gtk/src/gtk_s9x.cpp:568): every known key with its current value, aligned, with '  # comment' after some values; unknown keys and our comments are dropped (gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:205-394, conffile.cpp:124-220). The game-level restore runs after that exit, so it puts the pre-game value back into the rewritten file; the patcher's key regex takes the aligned leading spaces and the trailing comment as part of the line, and Snes9x's own parser strips the comment again (ConfigEntry::trimCommented, conffile.cpp:111). Separator ' = ' as Snes9x writes it (conffile.cpp:200, 202).

Sections and keys: section::key pairs in save_config_file/load_config_file (Display: gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:222-241 and 448-466; OpenGL: 256-257 and 482-483; Emulation: 316-319 and 539-542). Booleans: written true/false (SetBool with "true", "false", gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:210-211); read as true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off, anything else keeps the default (conffile.cpp:368-378).

renderer: [Display] HardwareAcceleration, a string: none, opengl, xv, vulkan (comment at gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:237; read 462; default opengl, 93). S9xInitDriver picks the driver once at startup: opengl, vulkan (USE_SLANG), xv (USE_XV + X11), anything else = the GTK/cairo software driver 'none' (gtk/src/gtk_display.cpp:911-940). If init fails it falls back to 'none' with a modal 'Couldn't load display driver' box (gtk_display.cpp:942-951). On a Wayland display everything but vulkan is forced to opengl (gtk_display.cpp:912-919), but RetroForge runs games on gamescope's Xwayland without WAYLAND_DISPLAY (rootfs/overlay/usr/bin/retroforge-session), so Software and XVideo are real. The pinned AppImage has XVideo built in (XvQueryAdaptors/XvShmPutImage in shared/bin/snes9x-gtk, libXv bundled) and the image's Xwayland has the XVideo extension; Snes9x lists xv only when an Xv adaptor is found (S9xXVDisplayDriver::query_availability, gtk_display.cpp:790-794): NOT HW-verified under gamescope (no adaptor = the error box, then Software).

aspect: three [Display] keys, all written by every choice. AspectRatio 0..5 (comment at gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:232; default 2, 86): 0/1 square pixels (256:224 = 8:7, 256:239 with ShowOverscanArea), 2/3 that x 7/6 = 4:3, 4/5 that x 8/7 = 64:49 'NTSC/PAL'; odd values = integer scale (S9xGetAspect and 'integer = aspect_ratio & 1', gtk/src/gtk_display.cpp:98-133). The ratio and the integer bit share one key, so integer scaling is folded into the aspect choices rather than a separate integer_scale option (two options cannot write one key). MaintainAspectRatio (default true, gtk_config.cpp:85) = false is the stretch: the image fills the window whatever AspectRatio says (S9xApplyAspect, gtk_display.cpp:136-196), so 'stretch' writes AspectRatio = 2 (the default) only to keep the same key set. ScaleToFit (default true, gtk_config.cpp:84) = false draws the game unscaled in the middle, which would make every choice here meaningless, so every choice writes ScaleToFit = true. Every driver goes through S9xApplyAspect (vulkan :204, opengl :87/:122, gtk :24, xv :121). Read at startup, applied on every frame.

smoothing: [Display] BilinearFilter (default false, gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:133; read 463). Used by OpenGL (GL_LINEAR/GL_NEAREST, gtk/src/gtk_display_driver_opengl.cpp:113), Vulkan (simple_output->set_filter, gtk/src/gtk_display_driver_vulkan.cpp:213; not when a custom shader is on, [OpenGL] EnableCustomShaders) and Software (cairo filter, gtk/src/gtk_display_driver_gtk.cpp:63-67). XVideo ignores it (the preferences dialog hides it for xv, gtk/src/gtk_preferences.cpp:191).

vsync: [OpenGL] VSync (sync_to_vblank, default true, gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:152; written 257, read 483). There is NO separate Vulkan key: the Vulkan driver uses the same sync_to_vblank (swapchain->set_vsync, gtk/src/gtk_display_driver_vulkan.cpp:89 and :225), OpenGL its swap interval (gtk/src/gtk_display_driver_opengl.cpp:362, :438). Software and XVideo do not use it. [Display] AutoVRR (default false, gtk_config.cpp:97) forces it on in fullscreen (gtk/src/gtk_s9xwindow.cpp:1211-1222); not touched.

show_fps: [Emulation] DisplayFrameRate (Settings.DisplayFrameRate, default false, gtk/src/gtk_config.cpp:167; written 319, read 542). Drawn by the ImGui OSD on Vulkan/OpenGL (external/imgui/snes9x_imgui.cpp:199) and into the emulated image otherwise (S9xDisplayMessages, gfx.cpp:2095-2096).

Left out: resolution (the SNES picture is 2D at native size; [Display] SoftwareScaleFilter is a 2x/xBRZ/HQ filter, a later 'shader'-like option, not an internal resolution), widescreen_hack (Snes9x has none), integer_scale (folded into aspect, above), frameskip (never: [Emulation] SpeedControlMethod is the pacing method and is not touched).
